protocol: loso_v2 folds 1/5/9 validation, per-record polarity/lag/amplitude diagnostics, evaluation only
role: Why does B1 performance differ so much across validation subjects?
reason: RESULT, 31 records. The heterogeneity is LAG, not polarity and not capability. corr(|lag|,PCC@0) = -0.898; corr(|lag|,bestPCC) = -0.125. Records with |lag|<=20ms (n=14) have PCC@0 median +0.571; records with |lag|>=45ms (n=13) have PCC@0 median -0.057 but bestPCC median +0.568 -- the SAME morphology quality. Median PCC@0 +0.220 vs median oracle-aligned bestPCC +0.635. Per-subject |lag| medians: S2 68ms (range 65-70, near-constant within subject), S13 12ms, S29 35ms (range 0-95 plus one 740ms outlier record MMECG_0059). Apparent polarity inversion is a consequence of a 65-70ms shift on a QRS-dominated signal, not sign flip. F1@100 stays 0.69-0.99 because a 100ms tolerance absorbs a 65ms lag, which is why rhythm looked recovered while PCC looked near zero. Over-smoothing is real but secondary: var_ratio median 0.599, corr(var_ratio,PCC@0) only +0.321. CAVEAT: bestPCC is obtained by aligning against the ground-truth ECG and is therefore ORACLE information; it bounds what is recoverable, it is not achievable performance. NO cross-subject mean is reported: subjects differ too much for an average to describe any of them.

protocol: loso_v2 folds 1/5/9, frozen checkpoints, four signed lag measurements + stratified correction, evaluation only
role: Lag provenance audit: is the residual offset real, where does it originate, is it correctable without oracle?
reason: SIGNED LAGS (val windows, ms): L1 radar->GT median -90 IQR 120 (xcorr ambiguity >0.8 in 26.2% of windows, so unreliable per-window); L2 event-head->GT +20 IQR 52.5; L3 waveform->GT +20 IQR 55; L4 waveform->event-head 0.0 IQR 0.0 MAD 0.0. L4=0 means the waveform and event head are perfectly co-aligned and carry the SAME offset, so self-correction from the event head is impossible. DECISIVE CONTRAST: TRAIN windows L3 median -5.0 IQR 10.0 vs VAL +20.0 IQR 55.0 -- the model is well-aligned on subjects it trained on and mis-aligned on held-out subjects, so the lag is a GENERALIZATION failure, not a fixed system offset. Per-subject val L3 medians: S2 +65 (n=170 windows, only 2 records -- NOT evidence of subject-level stability), S13 +5, S29 +20 (IQR 52.5). STRATIFIED PCC (per subject, records pooled, NO cross-subject mean): none -0.064/0.515/0.218; fixed-global (train-derived -5ms) -0.072/0.488/0.190 = WORSE than nothing on all three; oracle-per-record 0.537/0.616/0.602; oracle-per-window 0.584/0.666/0.651. Train-derived predictors all fail: state (train median -5ms for every state vs val -5/+30/+40/+12.5), HR (residual MAD 27.5ms vs 30.0ms for constant zero), radar anchor L1 (corr with L3 +0.066). Sync checks pass: end-start==1600 for all windows. ORACLE bestPCC IS A DIAGNOSTIC UPPER BOUND, NOT ACHIEVABLE PERFORMANCE. The earlier corr(|oracle lag|,PCC@0)=-0.898 is NOT used as proof of causation, since bestPCC is defined as the max over lag; the independent evidence is the peak-train offsets L2/L3 and the train-vs-val contrast.

protocol: loso_v2 folds 1/5/9, frozen B1, radar-only lag prediction; labels from TRAIN only; val ECG used only to score
role: Decisive test: is the timing offset predictable from radar alone?
reason: GATE FAILED on all three deployable arms. Required: all 3 subjects improve AND mean dPCC >= 0.08. Achieved: A1 train-median mean dPCC -0.009; A2 handcrafted radar features +0.009 (2/3 subjects up); A3 ridge on frozen encoder latent -0.008. Lag MAE (ms) S2/S13/S29: zero 66.0/22.1/41.0, handcrafted 68.8/21.6/39.1, frozen-ridge 72.1/24.4/39.3 -- all indistinguishable from predicting zero, several worse. UPPER BOUNDS ONLY: oracle-per-record dPCC +0.601/+0.101/+0.384, oracle-per-window +0.651/+0.153/+0.437, lag MAE 8.4/13.9/13.3. So the headroom is large and real but no radar-only route reaches any of it. With L4=0 from the provenance audit (event head perfectly co-aligned with the waveform, hence no internal signal), no route was found by the LINEAR/RIDGE readouts tested. SCOPE: this does not show the offset is unidentifiable from radar, nor that it is a deployment rather than modelling limit; both claims are withdrawn as overreach. The probe used only WSST-derived features, and WSST is |CWT|, a magnitude transform that discards phase. ALIGNMENT ROUTE TERMINATED per the pre-registered rule. Scope: linear/ridge readouts only, as specified; a deep nonlinear predictor is the excluded alignment network. n=3 subjects.
